summary: The recent arXiv window is dominated by theory and phenomenology rather than new heavy-ion experimental measurements. The strongest directly relevant heavy-ion paper is the WAGASHI event-generator study of non-perturbative quark production and transport in the glasma. Other useful items address quasi-hydrodynamic EFT from kinetic theory, magnetized-QGP photon production, nuclear many-body emulation, differentiable neutrino-analysis infrastructure, and scalable Bayesian calibration. Caution is warranted for rotating-QCD critical-exponent claims that remain mean-field-model limited and for broad generative-model unification whose transfer to HEP workflows is still mostly conceptual.
strongest_paper: arXiv:2608.13393, WAGASHI, because it combines event-by-event classical Yang-Mills glasma evolution, Wong-equation transport, and Schwinger quark-pair production into a concrete early-time heavy-ion modeling tool.

papers.title: Non-perturbative quark production and transport in the evolving glasma: the WAGASHI event generator
papers.authors_short: Nicholas J. Benoit, Chiho Nonaka, Hidetoshi Taya
papers.abstract: Develops WAGASHI, combining classical Yang-Mills glasma evolution, Wong-equation transport, and Schwinger pair production event by event. The authors report sizeable early quark production, momentum broadening, spin randomization, and event-by-event conserved-charge and polarization distributions for Pb-Pb and O-O at LHC energies.

papers.title: Effective field theory of quasi-hydrodynamics from kinetic theory
papers.abstract: Derives a systematic effective-field-theory framework for linear quasi-hydrodynamics from causal kinetic-like theories with slow degrees of freedom. The result places Israel-Stewart-like transient hydrodynamics in a universal slow-relaxation class with inherited causality, positivity, Onsager, and symmetry constraints.

papers.title: Magnetization and Magnetic Field-Induced Correction: Implications for QGP Thermal Photon Production in Magnetohydrodynamic
papers.authors_short: Jing Jing, Duan She, Ze-Fang Jiang
papers.abstract: Studies thermal photons from magnetized QGP in 1+1D relativistic MHD, including magnetic susceptibility and weak-field corrections to quark distributions. The work finds photon yields are mainly governed by initial field strength and decay, while weak-field distribution corrections enhance intermediate-pT photons.

papers.title: Parametric Matrix Models for Emulation in Nuclear and Many-Body Physics
papers.abstract: PhD thesis presenting parametric matrix models as interpretable, physically adjustable emulators for expensive nuclear and many-body calculations, with an accompanying GPU-optimized pyPMM package. The abstract emphasizes reduced-basis connections, modular deployment, and uncertainty-fitting workflows.

papers.title: MANGO: An Autodiff Neutrino Oscillation Engine for Differentiable Analysis Pipelines
papers.abstract: Introduces a differentiable neutrino-oscillation engine whose gradients pass through propagation geometry, Earth-shell densities, detector response, event weighting, binning, and likelihoods. Benchmarks against existing oscillation tools and finite differences are reported at high precision.

papers.title: Hierarchical Bayesian Calibration with Bayesian Committee Machine
papers.authors_short: Sebastian Heinekamp, David M. Higdon, Andreas Adelmann
papers.abstract: Develops hierarchical Bayesian calibration for repeated scientific experiments with experiment-specific parameters, using Bayesian Committee Machine Gaussian-process emulators for scalability and NUTS/automatic differentiation in Julia. Demonstrated on benchmarks and simulated Argonne Wakefield Accelerator data.

papers.title: Critical behavior and critical exponents of rotating QCD matter
papers.authors_short: Kai Xiao, Fei Sun, Shuang Li, Xun Chen
papers.abstract: Mean-field two-flavor NJL study of rotating strongly interacting matter and critical exponents near a CEP in the temperature-angular-velocity plane. The authors find mean-field scaling and argue rotation does not change the universality class within the model.

papers.title: Unifying Generative Models with Path Integrals
papers.abstract: Formulates flow, diffusion, variational, and adversarial generative models within a path-integral master-action language and reports one-loop corrections for deterministic samplers on controlled drifts. Cross-listed with hep-ph, but the immediate HEP/heavy-ion use case is still conceptual.
